summary: Will Sweetman is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge (~1988–1992) and held a post at the University of Otago (~2003).

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby (1933–2003) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Tamalpais High School, Stanford, Harvard (~1955–1958), and Princeton (~1958–1962), and held a position at the University of Toronto (~1971–1999).
Willard J. Peterson (born 1939) is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. Mentored by Denis Twitchett, he served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1981).

Willard Van Orman Quine (1908–2000) was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard, served in the U.S. Navy (1942–1945), and held posts at Harvard (1933–1978) and Wesleyan University (1964–1965).

Willem Bollée (1927–2020) was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (1975). He was an assistant professor at Münster (1971–1978) and professor at Heidelberg from 1979.

Willem Caland (1859–1932) worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Leiden University (~1877–1882), he served at Leiden (1913–1914) and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (~1906–1929; Professor 1906–1917).

Willem van der Molen (born 1952) specializes in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and held posts at Leiden (~1978–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William C. Kirby (born 1950) is a Sinologist and historian. He studied at Dartmouth College (~1968–1972) and Harvard University (~1973–1981), later holding a post at Harvard (~1992).

William Carey (1761–1834) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Sharma (~1796–1801). He founded the Serampore Mission Press and was Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College in 1801.
William Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles (-2006), where he studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and William M. Bodiford.

William Dwight Whitney (1827–1894) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Williams, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, Roth, and Bopp. He was a professor of Sanskrit at Yale (1853–1894) and served as president of the AOS.

William Edelglass works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007), served as a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013), and was a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.
William Erskine (1773–1852) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1788–1792).
William Frederic Sinclair (1847–1900) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and held a post in the Indian Civil Service beginning in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. (born 1943) is a Sinologist who studied at Bonn and Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He held appointments at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, including Halls-Bascom Professor (~2002).
William J. Johnson is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Cardiff University and the University of Wales (attested 1998).
William James (1842–1910) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Plymouth College and Harvard University (~1861–1869), he held a post at Harvard University from ~1872 to 1907.

William Jones (1746–1794) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow and Oxford. He became Chief Justice at the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (1783) and founded the Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He earned an M.S. from Caltech and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later holding posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University.

William L. Smith (born 1942) is an Indology scholar. He held appointments at Hampton University, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Stockholm University (~1980–2009).
